title: Integer coordinates of quotient generator germs
statement: Let X be a topological space and iota:K -> C a monomorphism of abelian sheaves, with C isomorphic to the constant integer sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let A_j, j in Fin n, be open sets, labels 0<c_j<=b+1, and g:coproduct_j j_{A_j!}Z -> K an epimorphism [def-sc-abelian-open-extension-by-zero]. Suppose component j sends its canonical unit section to s_j and iota(s_j) has constant integer value c_j. Let l:L -> K be any monomorphism. Fix x with zero L stalk [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] outside V=union_{c_j<=b} A_j, and an index i with x in A_i. Every element of the cokernel(l) stalk at x is a unique integer multiple of the germ of cokernel.π(l)(s_i).

proof.text: All indices active at x have label b+1, since a lower label would put x in V. The chosen active index ensures the family is nonempty.
Identify active extension-by-zero source stalks with integers generated by the unit germ, and inactive source stalks with zero.

Stalks preserve the coproduct and epimorphism g, so germs of active s_j generate K_x. Stalks preserve the monomorphism iota. Their images are all b+1 under canonical constant integer coordinates, so injectivity makes them equal. Because b+1 is nonzero, the common generator has infinite order. Every K_x element therefore has a unique integer coordinate.
Exactness of the abelian-sheaf stalk functor and L_x=0 imply that the cokernel projection is an isomorphism on stalks. Transport the unique integer coordinates along this projection.
